concept.title: Miscelllaneous style guides
concept.shortdesc: Beyond these named guides, many software companies maintain internal style guides for documentation and developer

conbody.p:
Beyond these named guides, many software companies maintain internal style guides for documentation and developer content, often modelled on or extended from CMOS or similar generalpurpose guides. These inhouse guides typically emphasize:
Consistent product naming, capitalization, and featurelabel wording.
A usercentric, activevoice writing style aligned with the company’s brand but still technically precise.

Whether you follow Google, IBM, Microsoft, CMOS, S1000D, or a custom style guide, the underlying principles remain the same. Your DITA style rules fit naturally into any of these ecosystems, while the style guide simply defines the “flavour” and formatting conventions on top.
